title: Policy & Procedure To Guide Use of Implantable Prosthesis and Medical Devices
html:
Policy & Procedure To

Guide Use of Implantable Prosthesis and Medical Devices

  • PURPOSE:
    • To provide guidelines on the procurement and usage of implantable prosthesis and medical devices.
  • SCOPE:
    • Purchase
    • Hospital Wide – All Inpatient care areas
  • RESPONSIBILTY:
    • Consultants / Doctors – Orthopedic Surgeons, Neuro Surgeons, Cardiologists
    • Medical Officers
    • OT In-Charge
    • Purchase In-Charge
  • ABBREVIATION:
    • NABH: National Accreditation Board For Hospitals and Healthcare providers
    • MOM: Management Of Medication
    • N.S : Nursing Staff
    • M.O.: Medical Officer
    • RMO: Resident Medical Officer
  • DEFINITION:
    • Nil.
  • REFERENCE: NABH
  • POLICY:
    • Hospital is committed to provide utmost safety of our patients undergoing implant procedures.
    • Strict guidelines are followed while buying the implants. Implantable prosthesis
    • A wide variety of implants are used for different purposes. They are metallic, bio-absorbable, non-metallic, non-absorbable (Ceramic, silicon, polyethylene, etc), bone graft substitutes, biochemical substances, PMMA, and silicon materials used in intraocular lenses, silicon materials used retinal surgery (Silicon oil, explants, bands, straps, clips etc) and glaucoma surgery devices (Aqueous drainage implants).
    • Selection of implantable prosthesis is based on scientific criteria and national/internationally recognized approvals (Drugs and Cosmetics Act notification Oct.2015/ US-FDA)
  • PROCEDURE:
    • Implant Procurement: It is our endeavor to see to the utmost safety of our patients undergoing implant procedures. We follow certain strict guidelines while buying the implants. Concerned doctors formulates and governs the rules and regulations of quality implant procurement. The highlights of the formulations are:
  • The retailer of the implant supply should have well experience in this field.
  • Pre gamma irradiated implants should not have any broken packages.
  • Implants should be free of scratches and transported in a hygienic environment.
  • Additional instrumentation required for the implantation should be supplied by the retailer.
  • Any damaged implants like scratches or slipped head screws should be replaced.
  • The hospital should have adequate stock of the implant at a given time.
  • The hospital must use rental systems for certain rare procedures.
    • Implant Maintenance: All implants are kept and stored in a sterile environment and re-sterilized once in 3 days if not used (gamma irradiated implants are exempted from this).
    • There shall be well trained staff and operation room personnel who keep constant vigil regarding safe and hygienic handling of these implants.
    • Implant sterilization: All implants are sterilized by autoclaved at 121 degrees C for 30 minutes except the gamma irradiated implants. Pre-sterilized or gamma irradiated implants are checked for damages in packing. Before sterilization the implants are subjected strict scrutiny to check for scratches, breakages and contamination.
    • Implant disposal: All implants recovered from the patient’s body are given back to the patient himself to prevent accidental or malafide re-use. In view of the patient’s health and well-being we do counseling regarding the implants and various merits and demerits using different type’s implants to be used in their bodies and the approximate time of removal of these implants from their bodies.
    • Documentation: The batch no, and serial no of the implantable prosthesis are recorded in the patient’s medical record and Operation Theatre and the discharge summary. The batch stickers are also applied in the respective areas.
    • Patient education: Every patient undergoing surgery for instillation of an implant or device shall be educated and oriented towards the safe usage and precautions to be taken by the concerned treating and operating doctors. The precautions shall include the aspects of non-usage of specific drugs, diet and reporting to the hospital in case certain specific symptoms are noticed.
